target_customer: Biopharma partners and drug developers working on protein therapeutics for cancer and autoimmune disease
problem: Potent protein drugs such as immunotherapies are too toxic because they act in healthy tissue; drugs that only turn on at diseased tissue would widen the therapeutic window.
business_model: Therapeutics platform; likely partnering or pipeline development (not stated)

founders.name: Elliot Tague
prior_employers: George Church lab at Harvard (visiting graduate student)
education: Boston University, PhD in biomedical engineering
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: worked at various biotech startups.

founders.name: Nathan Tague
education: PhD in biomedical engineering; school not stated
founders.background_notes: Brother of Elliot per YC page.

competitors.name: CytomX (Probody)
competitors.what: Protease-activated masked antibodies and cytokines active in tumor tissue
competitors.traction_then: Clinical-stage platform with 2023 conference data on masked interferon

technical_complexity.rationale: Engineering protein sensors that sense disease and gate a drug requires research-grade protein design and years of preclinical and clinical work.

defensibility.rationale: The YC launch post says the founders hold patent filings, but several clinical-stage firms already pursue conditional activation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows these firms copying or buying SynsoryBio.

market_need_then: Toxicity limits potent cancer immunotherapies, per the company's YC description; masked and conditionally active biologics were an active area with clinical programs by 2023.

branding.domain_note: Uses synsorybio.com with a Bio suffix.

identity.visual_style: Minimal site with a header image

brand_strength.rationale: A coined name suggesting sensing, easy to confuse with sensory or Sensory Inc, with no press or community. Biotech brand matters little at this stage.

outcome_analysis: SynsoryBio is an active two person biotech from YC Winter 2024 building conditionally activated protein drugs. Only a small grant and aggregator-reported pre-seed money were found. Biotech needs far more capital than the early rounds provide, so the key milestone is a priced seed or partnership, which is not yet sourced.
notes: Grant of 275K appears on HigherGov (aggregator of government awards) with no date or agency verified; Unverified and no longer recorded as a round, since HigherGov is an aggregator and a later search found no named outlet reporting any grant. VCBacked reports 500K pre-seed in April 2024 with Y Combinator and Unpopular Ventures, unverified. Competitor entries are platform companies active by 2023; two have undated sources. Undated competitors left out of the list: Werewolf Therapeutics, Xilio Therapeutics. Re-check: VCBacked (aggregator) 500K pre-seed April 2024 and Extruct (stage seed) were the only other funding mentions found; no non aggregator outlet states a round, so none is recorded. Update: the 500K pre-seed (April 2024) rests on a single database (VCBacked); CB Insights also shows 500K as a convertible note without a date. Cross-check found no press release.
